extracted.intended_audience: medical students, laboratory technicians, and bacteriology practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Practical manual of bacteriologic laboratory methods and procedural standards covering media preparation, sterilisation, inoculation, microscopy, animal experiments, and quantitative/qualitative analyses used in clinical and research labs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria of infection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This index entry labels a chapter/section that defines how infection is diagnosed/established; no procedural detail appears on this page (see referenced chapter for full criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion of immunity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index heading indicating standards for defining or measuring immunity; detailed definitions and tests are in the body text not present on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardisation of media and reagents
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardisation of media; Standardising bouillon; Standard graduated pipettes; Standard soda solution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to procedures and requirements for making, standardising, and using media and standard reagents. This page lists the topics only; the full methods, titration and acceptance criteria are in the corresponding chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sterilisation methods and agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterilisation by chemicals; by dry heat; by filters; by moist heat; by streaming steam; by superheated steam; of albuminous liquids; of gases; Sterilising agents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the recognised methods and classes of sterilisation to be used in bacteriologic work. The index lists the types but does not include stepwise protocols or performance criteria on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations and restrictions for laboratory animal use
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory animals, regulations; Restrictions upon experimental inoculations; Vivisection license; Preparation of experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates legal/ethical and institutional requirements governing use of animals, licences, and limits on inoculation experiments. The index provides headings; full regulatory text and restrictions are in the chapters referred to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination and control of media reaction and incubation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Titration of media; Estimation of reaction of media; Optimum reaction of medium; Range of medium reaction; Temperature — optimum and range; Pressure and temperature tables
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers measurement and control of pH/reaction and incubation temperature/pressure for cultures. The page shows topics and tables exist, but detailed measurement methods and acceptance ranges are in the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation, storage, and handling of culture media
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of nutrient media (bouillon, gelatine, agar etc.); Storage of media in bulk; Storing tubes of media; Sore boxes; Tubing of nutrient; Storage of stock nutrient media
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entries for procedures and storage requirements for various media types; specific recipes, storage conditions and shelf-life criteria appear in the relevant sections, not on this index page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of isolation and identification of bacteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of isolation (by plate cultures, by dilution, by differential atmosphere cultivation/incubation/media/sterilisation, by animal experiments); Methods of identification of bacteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists principal isolation and identification approaches used in bacteriology. This index shows the methods that are treated in the book; procedural specifics and diagnostic criteria are located in the referenced chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopy, fixation and staining standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopical examination of bacteria (stained and unstained); Fixation and fixing fluids for films; Staining methods (Gram, Ziehl-Neelsen, various capsule/flagella/spore stains); Mounting and permanent preparations; Measuring bacteria; Objectives, eyepieces, condensers, micrometers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects the optical and histologic techniques required for observation and measurement of microbes, including instruments and staining protocols. The page lists the topics; detailed staining recipes, fixation times, and optical performance criteria belong to the full methods chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample collection and handling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection of blood for bacteriological examination; Collection of milk samples; Collection of pathological material during life; Collection of pus; Collection of soil and water samples; Ice-box for water samples; Water collecting bottles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the types of clinical and environmental samples to be collected and implies proper containers/handling/storage topics; the index identifies these sections but full acceptance criteria and handling procedures are in the book's chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative and quantitative analysis procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative analysis of air, milk, sewage, soil, unsound meat, water; Quantitative analysis of air, milk, sewage, soil, unsound meat, water; Enumeration of micro-organisms; Counting plate colonies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that the manual covers both qualitative and quantitative analytical protocols and colony enumeration methods; the index does not reproduce the stepwise methods or analytical limits found in the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and manipulation of virulence and toxins
rubrics_metrics.description: Attenuating the virulence of organisms; Exalting/raising virulence of organisms; Toxins — extracellular/intracellular/soluble/insesparate; Testing of toxins; Minimal/lethal dose; Thermal death-point and coefficients of inhibition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists topics relating to virulence testing, toxin characterization, lethal-dose determinations and sterilisation/thermal death assessments. Detailed experimental designs, biosafety considerations, and acceptance criteria are not present on this page.
